phase: V0.3 Positive Growth Opportunity — Phase A

predefined_metrics.A: Strict same-user, same-session View Item → Add to Cart
predefined_metrics.B: Strict same-user, same-session Add to Cart → Begin Checkout
predefined_metrics.C: Strict same-user, same-session Begin Checkout → Purchase
predefined_metrics.F: First-session Activation Depth distribution (shallow, browse, intent); only intent share is a pre-specified positive-direction candidate component.

methodology.candidate_rule: Two complete baseline weeks followed by two consecutive complete growth weeks and a two-week confirmation period. Growth and confirmation must each be statistically positive versus baseline (two-sided pooled two-proportion z test, p < 0.05); each growth week must exceed aggregate baseline rate; each period must have at least 100 eligible observations.
methodology.confidence_intervals: 95% Wilson intervals for weekly and period rates.
methodology.selection_rule: Rank only candidates passing all gates, by data quality, minimum statistical strength across growth and confirmation, minimum period sample, two-week persistence, confirmation lift, and business relevance.

data_quality.structural_break_assessment: Primary event coverage is continuous. add_to_cart has an early zero-volume interval; metrics whose denominator or numerator requires add_to_cart exclude weeks before 2020-11-30.
data_quality.retention_right_censoring_control: Only first_visit cohorts through 2021-01-24 are used, so every retained cohort has seven follow-up days through 2021-01-31.

selected_candidate.metric_label: Strict same-user, same-session Begin Checkout → Purchase

segment_localization.scope: same-session metric; lifecycle is based on whether the investigated session contains first_visit
segment_localization.category_assessment: Not evaluated: category is not required to assess this metric's initial localization and would add high-cardinality exploratory noise.
segment_localization.composition_effect: Composition and within-segment effects are reported per dimension; neither is a causal attribution.
segment_localization.within_segment_effect: A positive within-segment comparison indicates an observed rate change after holding that dimension's observed mix fixed; it does not identify a mechanism.

evidence: Strict same-user, same-session Begin Checkout → Purchase increased from 40.35% in the baseline to 51.14% across two consecutive growth weeks.
The confirmation period was 55.07%, still above the baseline with a two-sided pooled proportion-test p-value of 7.22923e-12.
The selected comparison uses at least 670 eligible observations in each two-week period and excludes partial boundary weeks.
The scan used only pre-specified metrics and a deterministic six-week (baseline → growth → confirmation) window rule.
hypotheses: Observed within-segment change or traffic composition may be associated with the increase; the decomposition does not establish why the metric changed.
The persisted improvement may be compatible with a repeatable opportunity, but only a separate replication or controlled test could distinguish mechanism from temporal coincidence.
unknowns: Whether campaigns, merchandising, pricing, inventory, seasonality, product experience, or measurement conditions caused the observed change.
Whether the pattern will recur in an independent later period or outside this obfuscated public sample.
Whether dimensions not evaluated in this bounded Phase A scan would alter the descriptive localization.
suggested_future_evidence: REPLICATION_TEST: reproduce the observed window on an independent fully observed period before considering a controlled scale test; do not infer an intervention from this descriptive scan.
non_causal_boundary: This is a descriptive, read-only exploration. No causal root cause, intervention recommendation, production enum, or product logic is asserted or changed.
